results.question: In the cross-sectional pilot study of veterans, what cardiac MRI findings in people living with HIV suggested myocardial fibrosis and subclinical dysfunction?
results.answer: The study reports: "We found higher growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15 blood levels, increased extracellular volume, and lower right heart function on MRI among patients with HIV, suggesting the presence of increased myocardial fibrosis and subclinical myocardial dysfunction in this population." [PMID:41791688]. The study reports: "Limited data from this pilot study suggest that HIV may be associated with increased cardiac fibrosis and decreased right ventricular function." [PMID:41791688]. The study reports: "Multivariable linear regressions were used to investigate the associations. 21 veterans with HIV (mean age 54 years; 71% White, 29% Black) and 20 controls (mean age 56 years; 70% White, 30% Black) were included." [PMID:41791688]. The study reports: "We conducted a cross-sectional pilot study of matched veterans with and without HIV receiving care at the Providence VA Medical Center to explore the relationship between systemic inflammation, myocardial fibrosis, and subclinical cardiac disease in HIV." [PMID:41791688]. The study reports: "This study highlights the need for larger longitudinal studies to better understand the trajectory of HIV-associated cardiac changes and help improve cardiac disease prevention in this population." [PMID:41791688].

notes: The source quotations retain increased extracellular volume, lower right-heart MRI function and the suggestive rather than causal interpretation, with the 21/20 matched pilot population. Additional design and longitudinal-study quotations are supported but verbose.

results.question: How was SCAR-Net built and validated for distinguishing postoperative breast scars from recurrent lesions, and how much did it change radiologist performance?
results.answer: The study reports: "This study introduces SCAR-Net, a deep learning model specifically designed for ultrasound-based discrimination between these similar-appearing tissues." results.question: How did the fMRI acceleration method and the MR anisotropic-diffusion filters address different image-reconstruction problems, and what validation result did each report?
results.answer: The study reports: "Traditional MRI methodologies require full k-space information, which follows a unique data acquisition sequence to reconstruct the complete image." [PMID:41951145]. The study reports: "This process presents a time-consuming obstacle for medical imaging techniques." [PMID:41951145]. The study reports: "Our study proposes a novel image reconstruction method to enhance the efficiency of data acquisition while maintaining high accuracy in activation detection." [PMID:41951145]. The study reports: "The through-plane and in-plane acceleration techniques are combined to accelerate image acquisition along two dimensions." [PMID:41951145]. The study reports: "Multiple image-shift strategies and a 2D Hadamard encoding scheme are used to increase encoding diversity and reduce slice leakage." [PMID:41951145]. By applying this approach to both simulated and experimental fMRI data, the study reported reduced total scan time while achieving a higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in regions of interest (ROI). Compared with conventional reconstruction strategies, the proposed method demonstrated potential improvements in activation detection under specific acceleration and encoding conditions, while also providing voxel-wise estimates through a Bayesian framework [PMID:41951145]. The study reports: "Due to the inherent correlation between Rice's noise and the Magnetic Resonance (MR) signal that occurs during the MR images formation, denoising these images is an important but complex process, as it can prove insufficient and even result in the loss of information details." [PMID:41903663]. The study reports: "To overcome these two drawbacks, filtering methods based on Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) have been introduced, but the parameters of the filters they propose must be determined with great accuracy." [PMID:41903663]. The study reports: "In fact, in order to denoise MR images with high Rice's noise levels, we propose adapted filtering anisotropic diffusion PDE filter models by using precise local parameters adjustment." [PMID:41903663]. The study reports: "These filtering models incorporate a robust Rician noise estimator and an unbiased variant of filters based on anisotropic diffusion, whose parameters are all calculated simultaneously and optimized adaptively through the introduction of the PSO algorithm and the use of reference-based and no-reference quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM and Blind/Referenceless Image Spatial Quality Evaluator (BRISQUE))." [PMID:41903663]. The study reports: "Three unbiased anisotropic diffusion filtering models with optimized parameters for Rician noise removing in MR images.." [PMID:41903663]. The various tests performed on synthetic and real MR images provided excellent results compared to some other published methods, thus demonstrating the high performance of the proposed anisotropic diffusion filters in terms of noise reduction and preservation of important details [PMID:41903663].

notes: Both methods retain their required steps and distinct validation settings: through/in-plane acceleration, image shifts and 2D Hadamard with simulated and experimental fMRI; Rician noise estimation, adaptive PSO diffusion parameters and synthetic/real MR tests. Bayesian and activation-detection details are supported by the full source, without cross-study superiority. Many background sentences and a title make the answer unnecessarily long.
